place.why: University Hospital of Wales in Cardiff, Wales; A&E/Emergency Unit wording suggests NHS/public care.

summary: Your A&E care was NHS/public care run by Cardiff and Vale University Health Board, so you start by complaining to that Health Board under Wales’ NHS complaints process. If you are not satisfied, you can go to the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales, and if compensation is in issue there is a Wales redress route inside the complaint system for lower-value cases plus the usual court claim route with a 3-year time limit. Legal aid for an adult wrist-misdiagnosis claim is usually not in scope, so most people would look at the Health Board’s redress route or a no-win-no-fee solicitor.

Cardiff and Vale’s page still points patients to a detailed complaint form by email/post/phone, while the Welsh Government’s March 2026 people’s guidance says concerns now follow the two-stage 'Listening to People' process.
steps.deadline: "You can take up to 12 months to raise a concern or complaint."

points: University Hospital of Wales Emergency Unit is on the Cardiff and Vale University Health Board NHS site.
You can complain by phone, email, post, or by downloading the Health Board’s detailed complaint form; there is no working online complaint form on the site.
If you send the form by email, the provider says you will get an acknowledgement within two working days.
The Welsh Government says you can take up to 12 months to raise a concern or complaint.
From April 2026, Stage 1 is early resolution for no longer than 10 working days from acknowledgement; if not resolved, it moves to Stage 2 investigation including possible redress.
The public guidance says you should be given an estimated timescale for the initial investigation and response at Stage 2.
steps.appliesIf: NHS/public care at University Hospital of Wales, run by Cardiff and Vale University Health Board.
alternatives: You can first raise the issue informally with staff involved in your care.
If unhappy after the Health Board’s response, you can escalate to the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales.

steps.what: If the Health Board’s answer is not good enough, the independent body is the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales. You normally have to complain to the Health Board first, and the Ombudsman has an online complaint checker/form route.
steps.deadline: "We can look at complaints made to us within one year of the matters complained about (or within one year of you becoming aware of the issue)."
points: You must first complain to the organisation you are unhappy about.
The Ombudsman can look at complaints made within one year of the matters complained about, or within one year of becoming aware of the issue.
If the events were more than a year ago but you complained to the Health Board in time, you should complain to the Ombudsman within 12 weeks of the Health Board or Trust’s response.
The Ombudsman says the NHS body usually aims to respond in about 6 weeks but can take up to 6 months for more complex complaints, and it is unlikely to consider the case before then.
The online route starts with a complaint checker asking what type of body you want to complain about.
They also offer help by phone and support in another language.

Usually wait for the Health Board’s response or for the Health Board to have had up to 6 months to respond.
steps.appliesIf: You remain unhappy with the outcome of an NHS/public complaint in Wales.
alternatives: You can seek legal advice about a compensation claim instead of, or as well as, pursuing an ombudsman complaint, but the ombudsman route is for independent complaint review rather than damages.

steps.body: Welsh NHS redress scheme under the National Health Service (Concerns, Complaints and Redress Arrangements) (Wales) Regulations
steps.what: For NHS/public care in Wales, compensation can begin inside the NHS complaints process: if the Welsh NHS body investigating the concern decides a qualifying liability exists or may exist, it must consider whether to offer redress. From 1 April 2026 the amending regulations raise the redress compensation cap from £25,000 to £50,000; if the value is above that, compensation should be pursued outside the redress part of the scheme, usually by a court claim.
steps.deadline: "the period applicable is three years from—"
points: A Welsh NHS body must consider redress when, during a regulation-23 investigation, it decides a qualifying liability exists or may exist.
The 2011 regulations allow financial compensation under redress up to £25,000, but the 2025 amending regulations substitute £50,000 from 1 April 2026.
If the Welsh NHS body thinks the value exceeds the cap, financial compensation must not be offered under the redress part of the scheme.
If redress is being considered, legal advice must be available to the person seeking redress, and the Welsh NHS body bears those legal and jointly instructed expert costs.
A court clinical-negligence/personal-injury claim is generally subject to a 3-year limitation period from the cause of action or the later date of knowledge.
requires: First notify the concern to the Welsh NHS body through the complaint/Listening to People process if you want the in-scheme redress route.
For a court claim, you will usually need specialist legal advice and evidence on breach of duty and causation.
steps.appliesIf: NHS/public care in Wales; the in-scheme redress route applies only if the responsible Welsh NHS body identifies a qualifying liability and the case value is within the scheme cap.
alternatives: If the case is worth more than the redress cap, or the NHS body does not offer redress, you can pursue a court clinical-negligence claim.
You can still complain even if you also take legal advice.
missing: Whether the patient wants to pursue complaint-only redress, a solicitor-led court claim, or both.
The scale of financial losses and prognosis after surgery, which may affect valuation.
Any later provider response or admission of fault.

sources.quote: Where an investigation of a concern is being undertaken in accordance with regulation 23 by a responsible body that is a Welsh NHS body and the Welsh NHS body determines that a qualifying liability exists or may exist, it must, in accordance with the provisions of this Part, determine whether or not an offer of redress should be made to the patient.
A Welsh NHS body may make an offer of redress for a qualifying liability by way of financial compensation in which the sum does not exceed £25,000.

Where a Welsh NHS body considers that the value to be attributed to the qualifying liability exceeds £25,000, redress in the form of financial compensation must not be offered in accordance with this Part.
In regulation 29(1) and (2) (redress – financial compensation), for “£25,000” substitute “£50,000”.
The cost of such legal advice and costs arising from the instruction of such medical experts must be borne in their entirety by the Welsh NHS body.

steps.body: Legal Aid / conditional fee funding in England and Wales
steps.what: For an adult wrist-misdiagnosis claim like this, ordinary civil legal aid is not the main route: the clinical-negligence scope in LASPO is tightly limited to severe neurological injury caused before birth or within the short period after birth. An out-of-scope case can still seek exceptional case funding if refusing legal aid would breach human-rights-based rights, and private funding by 'no win, no fee' is allowed, with the success fee capped in personal injury claims.
points: The statutory legal-aid scope for clinical negligence is limited to neurological injury causing severe disability, with the negligence occurring in the womb or during/after birth within the specified early period.
Exceptional case funding may be available for a case that would not usually be eligible if human rights are at risk and the person is financially eligible.
The official legal aid adviser finder lets you search for clinical-negligence legal aid advisers in England and Wales.
No win no fee success fees in personal injury claims are capped at 25% of specified damages, excluding future pecuniary loss and subject to the first-instance limitation in the Order.
The Law Society’s official free finder can be used to look for a solicitor by legal issue and location if you want a private or CFA-funded lawyer.
steps.appliesIf: England and Wales funding rules, including Wales NHS clinical-negligence claims.
alternatives: Wales redress cases may include legal advice paid by the Welsh NHS body if the redress scheme is engaged.
A private retainer is another alternative if legal aid and CFA are not suitable.
missing: Your finances, if you want to explore exceptional case funding or any remaining legal-aid possibility.
Whether you want a legal-aid search, a no-win-no-fee search, or both.
